technologies.label: Bionics
technologies.scope: From cells, organs, individual human organisms and engineered biological intelligence to ecosystems and the planetary biosphere.
technologies.note: Deliberately broader than the everyday use of the word for prosthetics: technology working through biological systems, whether restoring an ecosystem or augmenting a human. This is the new paradigm shift this issue introduces.

technologies.label: Psychotronics
technologies.scope: From individual consciousness and PSI to collective and noöspheric phenomena and the setting's Source Consciousness field.
technologies.note: Already established as a paradigm; the #345 track owns its detail.

technologies.label: Cybernetics
technologies.scope: From prosthetics, BCIs and local computing to AI, networks, autonomous systems and sociotechnical infrastructure.
technologies.note: The cybernetic/social correspondence is a game-design abstraction, NOT a claim that Luhmann's social communication is identical to computers. Keep the distinctive Luhmannian distinction between biological, psychic and social systems.

system_distinction.note: Three interacting domains, never three exclusive tech trees. The Luhmannian distinction between biological, psychic and social systems is a setting-level commitment; the systems-correspondence table is a design abstraction and must not be read as identifying social communication with computation.

framing.primary: New Weird + science fiction comedy + social science fiction / science fantasy, with Cyberpunk influence
framing.rule: genres overlap without spawning separate game systems
framing.note: The six genres are setting descriptors, technological aesthetics and political-conflict framings. No genre adds its own rules subsystem.

genres.label: Biopunk
genres.definition: Biotechnology and living systems from personal augmentation to restored or devastated planetary ecology.
conflicts: biosphere survival versus runaway ecologies and engineered pandemics
corporate patent monopolies over engineered life
green primitivists versus biotech eco-modernists versus communitarian solarpunks versus corporate greenwashing

genres.label: Solarpunk
genres.definition: Ecological regeneration, distributed renewable energy, circular production, low-impact architecture, local food production, resilient communities and commons-based technology.
genres.note: Not simply an idyllic aesthetic: a political counterproject to extractive accelerationism, planetary ecological collapse and authoritarian control.

genres.label: Nanopunk
genres.definition: Nanoscale engineering transforms matter, medicine, manufacturing, weapons and ecology, connecting cybernetic, biological and potentially psychotronic technologies.
genres.note: A clear progression from established nanoscience to fictional high-end molecular assemblers. Grey-goo disasters, ecological contamination, surveillance dust and nano-enabled NHI technologies provide crises, but need not define the entire field.

genres.label: PSIpunk
genres.definition: PSI and noetic technology transform institutions, politics, policing, crime, intimacy, privacy, hacking, ideology and warfare; consciousness and Source Consciousness are integral to the setting's worldview.
genres.note: An explicit NoöPunk genre, NOT a new paradigm shift: PSI and psychotronics already exist as a paradigm.
conflicts: how PSI changes institutions, evidence, criminal strategy and class structure rather than merely providing special attacks

genres.label: UFOpunk
genres.definition: Disclosure, UAP sightings, crash retrieval, cover-ups, abductions, contact, ontological shock, rival intelligence services, uncertainty about NHI origins, and ordinary people adapting to reality breaking.
genres.note: Internal NoöPunk definition. No widely established, standardised genre canon for the name was found, so it is recorded as a useful internal descriptor rather than asserted as an established school. Surveillance, politics, secrecy and competing contact narratives are core.

genres.label: Xenopunk
genres.definition: Alien, interdimensional, extratemporal and cryptoterrestrial intelligence; interspecies societies, xenobiology, hybridisation, asymmetric contact, linguistic and political difference, and coexistence versus assimilation and exploitation.
genres.note: Internal NoöPunk definition, for the same reason as UFOpunk: no widely established genre canon for the name was found, so no established school is claimed.

epistemic_rule.note: Issue #359: distinguish actual investigators and their hypotheses from NoöPunk fiction, where PSI and psychotronic paradigm shifts are settled features of the game world. Real early research is inspiration for extrapolation in a science-fiction RPG, and present-day scientific limits are not imposed on the setting's later paradigm shifts - but a research tradition must never be recorded as an achieved capability.
epistemic_rule.enforced_as: every research-kind inspiration must carry a declared capability_status; one that does not is reported by the reader as an unearned capability claim
